meta.title: Client-side rate limiting
meta.head: rate-limit
meta.pr: Add client-side rate limiting to the API client (stops rate-limit errors)

C1.label: verified
C1.claim: `RateLimiter` is a token bucket: it stores at most `burst` tokens and refills `rate` tokens per second.

C2.label: verified
C2.claim: The constructor raises `ValueError` for a `rate` of zero or less, or a `burst` below 1.

C3.label: verified
C3.claim: `acquire` refills the bucket from the elapsed time, capped at `burst`, and takes a token at once when at least 1 is available.

C4.label: verified
C4.claim: When no token is available, `acquire` works out the wait as the missing part of a token divided by `rate`, sets the bucket to zero, and sleeps after the lock is released.

C5.label: inferred
C5.claim: Several threads can share one bucket without spending the same token twice: `_lock` guards the arithmetic, the sleep happens outside it, and a later caller sees a stamp in the future and waits longer.
C5.why: Lines 19 to 28 run inside the with block; line 28 stores a future time in _stamp, so the next caller's elapsed time is negative and its wait grows; line 29 sleeps after the block ends. Together this queues callers in order.

C7.label: verified
C7.claim: `Client` builds one `RateLimiter` from the config's rate and burst when it is created, and `get` calls `acquire` before it builds the request.

C8.label: inferred
C8.claim: Each `Client` makes its own `RateLimiter`, so two clients in one process each get the full rate: the limit is per client, not per process.
C8.why: Line 11 constructs the limiter inside the constructor, once per instance, and nothing in the diff passes one limiter to several clients.

C9.label: inferred
C9.claim: `get` waits inside `acquire` for as long as the bucket needs; nothing limits the wait, so a slow refill stalls the calling thread.
C9.why: acquire sleeps for the computed wait (line 29) and has no timeout or way to refuse; get (line 14) calls it directly.

C10.label: verified
C10.claim: The new tests cover a free burst of 3 calls, a fourth call that waits, and the `ValueError` for `rate=0`.

C11.label: inferred
C11.claim: No test covers the client calling the limiter, refill over time, or two threads sharing a bucket.
C11.why: The three tests only build a RateLimiter and call acquire; the client test file is not in the diff.

C12.label: verified
C12.claim: api/__init__.py changes spacing only: a blank line is added and a space after a comma; the exported names are the same.

C14.label: unverified
C14.claim: Whether the defaults match the provider's real limit is not stated anywhere in the repository.

C15.label: stated
C15.claim: The PR title says client-side limiting stops rate-limit errors. The code only spaces calls from one client; it never reads a failed response or a retry header.

change.purpose: Make the API client wait on a token bucket before each request, so one client never sends faster than its configured rate.

flow.text: caller -> `get` -> `acquire` (waits if the bucket is empty) -> the request -> server.
